content.text:
Render job: Look at the piece, ask me at most three quick questions, then place the cameras for a shot set and any animations, check the framing, render each take, look at it, re-render what falls short, and hand the set over for review. Render at draft quality.

Plan:
1. Look at the piece and any shot references; ask what the images are for
2. Place each camera and the look; check the framing
3. Render the stills and animations, look at each, re-render what falls short
4. You review the set: swap, star, choose the cover

# Canon canon-1e0781375cebc5 · ring/solitaire/0046d2982f30c2
## Rules (typical [band]; warnings give the reason)
- ring.solitaire.bandWidth (ringShank.widthTop) 1.93 [1.5–2.9]: The band frames the stone: under 1.8 mm reads fragile and bends, over 2.4 mm on a 1 ct swamps it. Delicate needs W ≤ 6.5.
- ring.solitaire.elevation (gem.placement.elevation) 2.3 [0.5–2.6]: Classic sits 0.2–0.8 mm above the band; low (0.8–1.2) only in a basket or bezel; above 4 mm it catches on everything.
- ring.solitaire.tableHeight (tableHeight) 6.26 [4.46–8.19]: Height is what the hand feels: 6–7 mm for a classic 1 ct, 7 for everyday, 10.5 only for a cocktail ring.
- ring.solitaire.widthBottom (ringShank.widthBottom) 2 [1.8–2.2]: Band width at the base
- ring.solitaire.thicknessTop (ringShank.thicknessTop) 1.8 [1.7–1.9]: Band thickness under the head
- bezel.wall (setting.wall) 0.7 [0.6–0.8]: The wall grows with the stone: 0.5–0.6 mm to 5 mm, 0.6–0.8 to 7, 0.7–1.0 above; +0.2 in 22k. Under 0.45 it will not cast.
- ring.scale.headToFinger (headToFinger) 0.55 [0.3–0.8]: Head to finger
- stones.oneHero (secondStone) 4.51 [0–5.47]: One stone must win in a blink: the second-largest at most 0.85 of the hero, or the eye cannot settle.
- ring.solitaire.thicknessBottom (ringShank.thicknessBottom) 1.6 [1.5–1.8]: Band thickness at the base
- ring.base.euro (euroBase) 0 [0–1]: Euro base for big heads
- stones.softInPave (softestInPave) 10 [8–10]: Flush, channel, bar and pavé stones take the knocks face-on: only Mohs 8 and harder survive them.
- metals.colours (metalColours) 1 [1–2]: Unity: one or two metal colours. Three reads as three pieces fighting.
- metals.finishes (finishCount) 1 [1–2]: Unity: at most two finishes, used to separate planes; more is noise.
- rows.coverage (gemRow.coverage) 160 [120–270]: Coverage of a part row
- ring.scale.stoneToFinger (stoneToFinger) 0.42 [0.3–0.65]: Stone to finger
- stones.meleeColour (meleeColourGap) 1 [0–2]: Melee colour against the centre
- metals.tipFamily (tipFamilies) 1 [1–1]: One claw-tip family
- iced.levels (levelStep) 1.2 [0.8–1.5]: Steps between levels
- stones.whiteHead (colourlessInYellowHead) 0 [0–0]: White head for colourless stones
## Style: Minimal
Reads right: Proportion and weight are the design: nothing hides a bad number. One finish, one metal, one stone or none. Low profiles and closed shapes: bezels, cigar bands, plain court.
Do: Set low. Keep to one finish. Check every proportion twice: there is nowhere to hide.
Don't: Halos or pavé shoulders. Two metals. Decoration that does not carry the stone.
- ringShank.widthTop 1.9 [1.8–2]: or a 5–8 mm cigar band
- setting.wall 0.6 [0.5–0.7]
- setting.prongDiameter 1 [0.9–1.1]: four claws on 6.5 mm
- gem.placement.elevation 1 [0.5–1.2]: low, in a basket or bezel
## Exemplars
- sol-minimal-bezel, Low bezel solitaire (solitaire, classic; minimal): metal au18k-yellow, cut round, head bezel, W 6.44, bandW 1.9, bandT 1.9, e 1, wall 0.6
  Why: A closed 0.6 mm bezel set low: nothing to snag, one clean line. Band 1.9 mm, one metal, one finish: proportion is the whole design. Table under 5 mm off the finger. Bad twin: A wall too thin to close over the girdle.
- sol-delicate-oval, Delicate oval solitaire (solitaire, delicate; delicate): metal au18k-yellow, cut oval, head basket, W 5.09, bandW 1.65, bandT 1.7, e 2.2, wire 0.95, prongs 4
  Why: A 1.65 mm band is only right under a stone of 6.5 mm or less: here 5.1 mm. The narrow band is nearly as deep as it is wide, so the head cannot twist it. North-south oval at 1.4 L:W lengthens the finger. Bad twin: A heavy band that swamps a small oval.
- sol-retro-cocktail, Two-tone aquamarine cocktail ring (solitaire, bold; retro, cocktail): metal au18k-rose, cut emerald, head basket, W 10.5, bandW 7, bandT 2.5, e 3, wire 1.5, prongs 4
  Why: A wide rose band that tapers to 3.5 mm carries a 10.5 mm stone like a 1940s tank ring. Heavy 1.5 mm claws and a euro base keep a big step cut upright. One alloy: a yellow head would be soldered on, which the kernel cannot check yet. Bad twin: Claws too fine for a 10 mm stone.
## Cannot build: say so, offer the stand-in
- French and U-cut pavé → build shared prong and say the setter will cut it
- Half-bezel arc other than 110° → the arc is fixed at 110° a side: a wider or narrower grip is a maker note
- Antique and fancy cuts → old European, rose, polki, tapered baguette, trapezoid and half-moon are not cuts here: name the stand-in
- Alloys and finishes we cannot specify → 21k, enamel, per-region plating and hand engraving: pick the nearest alloy and note the rest
## Watch for
- A stone row running into the head
- Fat claws that hide the stone
- A "lollipop" head: a big head on a stick of a shank
- Band and stone out of scale with each other
- A dead under-gallery: bare claws or a solid block from the side
## Ask (at most three)
- Ring size?
- Centre stone: shape, size or carat, natural or lab?
- Metal, and active hands or a flush-fit wedding band beside it?

## Rules (typical [band]; warnings give the reason)
- ring.solitaire.bandWidth (ringShank.widthTop) 1.93 [1.5–2.9]: The band frames the stone: under 1.8 mm reads fragile and bends, over 2.4 mm on a 1 ct swamps it. Delicate needs W ≤ 6.5.
- ring.solitaire.elevation (gem.placement.elevation) 2.3 [0.5–2.6]: Classic sits 0.2–0.8 mm above the band; low (0.8–1.2) only in a basket or bezel; above 4 mm it catches on everything.
- ring.solitaire.tableHeight (tableHeight) 6.26 [4.46–8.19]: Height is what the hand feels: 6–7 mm for a classic 1 ct, 7 for everyday, 10.5 only for a cocktail ring.
- ring.solitaire.widthBottom (ringShank.widthBottom) 2 [1.8–2.2]: Band width at the base
- ring.solitaire.thicknessTop (ringShank.thicknessTop) 1.8 [1.7–1.9]: Band thickness under the head
- bezel.wall (setting.wall) 0.7 [0.6–0.8]: The wall grows with the stone: 0.5–0.6 mm to 5 mm, 0.6–0.8 to 7, 0.7–1.0 above; +0.2 in 22k. Under 0.45 it will not cast.
- ring.scale.headToFinger (headToFinger) 0.55 [0.3–0.8]: Head to finger
- stones.oneHero (secondStone) 4.51 [0–5.47]: One stone must win in a blink: the second-largest at most 0.85 of the hero, or the eye cannot settle.
- ring.solitaire.thicknessBottom (ringShank.thicknessBottom) 1.6 [1.5–1.8]: Band thickness at the base
- ring.base.euro (euroBase) 0 [0–1]: Euro base for big heads
- stones.softInPave (softestInPave) 10 [8–10]: Flush, channel, bar and pavé stones take the knocks face-on: only Mohs 8 and harder survive them.
- metals.colours (metalColours) 1 [1–2]: Unity: one or two metal colours. Three reads as three pieces fighting.
- metals.finishes (finishCount) 1 [1–2]: Unity: at most two finishes, used to separate planes; more is noise.
- rows.coverage (gemRow.coverage) 160 [120–270]: Coverage of a part row
- ring.scale.stoneToFinger (stoneToFinger) 0.42 [0.3–0.65]: Stone to finger
- stones.meleeColour (meleeColourGap) 1 [0–2]: Melee colour against the centre
- metals.tipFamily (tipFamilies) 1 [1–1]: One claw-tip family
- iced.levels (levelStep) 1.2 [0.8–1.5]: Steps between levels
- stones.whiteHead (colourlessInYellowHead) 0 [0–0]: White head for colourless stones
## Style: Minimal
Reads right: Proportion and weight are the design: nothing hides a bad number. One finish, one metal, one stone or none. Low profiles and closed shapes: bezels, cigar bands, plain court.
Do: Set low. Keep to one finish. Check every proportion twice: there is nowhere to hide.
Don't: Halos or pavé shoulders. Two metals. Decoration that does not carry the stone.
- ringShank.widthTop 1.9 [1.8–2]: or a 5–8 mm cigar band
- setting.wall 0.6 [0.5–0.7]
- setting.prongDiameter 1 [0.9–1.1]: four claws on 6.5 mm
- gem.placement.elevation 1 [0.5–1.2]: low, in a basket or bezel
## Exemplars
- sol-minimal-bezel, Low bezel solitaire (solitaire, classic; minimal): metal au18k-yellow, cut round, head bezel, W 6.44, bandW 1.9, bandT 1.9, e 1, wall 0.6
  Why: A closed 0.6 mm bezel set low: nothing to snag, one clean line. Band 1.9 mm, one metal, one finish: proportion is the whole design. Table under 5 mm off the finger. Bad twin: A wall too thin to close over the girdle.
- sol-delicate-oval, Delicate oval solitaire (solitaire, delicate; delicate): metal au18k-yellow, cut oval, head basket, W 5.09, bandW 1.65, bandT 1.7, e 2.2, wire 0.95, prongs 4
  Why: A 1.65 mm band is only right under a stone of 6.5 mm or less: here 5.1 mm. The narrow band is nearly as deep as it is wide, so the head cannot twist it. North-south oval at 1.4 L:W lengthens the finger. Bad twin: A heavy band that swamps a small oval.
- sol-retro-cocktail, Two-tone aquamarine cocktail ring (solitaire, bold; retro, cocktail): metal au18k-rose, cut emerald, head basket, W 10.5, bandW 7, bandT 2.5, e 3, wire 1.5, prongs 4
  Why: A wide rose band that tapers to 3.5 mm carries a 10.5 mm stone like a 1940s tank ring. Heavy 1.5 mm claws and a euro base keep a big step cut upright. One alloy: a yellow head would be soldered on, which the kernel cannot check yet. Bad twin: Claws too fine for a 10 mm stone.
## Cannot build: say so, offer the stand-in
- French and U-cut pavé → build shared prong and say the setter will cut it
- Half-bezel arc other than 110° → the arc is fixed at 110° a side: a wider or narrower grip is a maker note
- Antique and fancy cuts → old European, rose, polki, tapered baguette, trapezoid and half-moon are not cuts here: name the stand-in
- Alloys and finishes we cannot specify → 21k, enamel, per-region plating and hand engraving: pick the nearest alloy and note the rest
## Watch for
- A stone row running into the head
- Fat claws that hide the stone
- A "lollipop" head: a big head on a stick of a shank
- Band and stone out of scale with each other
- A dead under-gallery: bare claws or a solid block from the side
## Ask (at most three)
- Ring size?
- Centre stone: shape, size or carat, natural or lab?
- Metal, and active hands or a flush-fit wedding band beside it?
